overall_summary: Analysis across 47 deduplicated Shorts reveals a distinct performance divide. The channel's strongest drivers are extreme exoplanet and extreme cosmic 'What If You Fell Into...' simulation hooks (consistently generating 800–1,050+ views and 20–38 likes per video, with 21-second runtimes). Conversely, recycled low-stakes psychology facts, repetitive biology snippets, and duplicate re-uploads (e.g., repeating 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' or 'Why Space Is Completely Silent') suffer severe algorithmic decay, averaging under 100 views and near-zero engagement.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Survival / 'What If You Fell Into...' Extreme Celestial Phenomena
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles using 'What If You Fell Into...' (IYuce8vaU3Y at 1,029 views, 38 likes; 8KEl0_pJ_68 at 974 views, 18 likes; YlDuGu1vzAg at 829 views, 15 likes) massively outperform descriptive fact titles.
winning_patterns.action: Adopt visceral second-person survival framing ('What If You...') paired with extreme, hostile cosmic or planetary environments at optimal 20-21 second runtimes.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (v1,032 views, 36 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies' (725 views, 25 likes) hold the highest like-to-view ratios (>3.5%).
winning_patterns.action: Highlight sensory and tangible planetary anomalies (liquid gem rain, absolute darkness, kinetic atmospheric extremes) with rich cinematic visualization.

weak_patterns.pattern: Repetitive Trivia Re-uploads & Generic Brain Psychology
weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 to 53 views) and 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' (34 to 220 views) generate virtually zero comments and negligible likes.
weak_patterns.action: Completely halt identical/rephrased re-uploads; retire generic human brain trivia unless framed through high-stakes psychological survival or micro-mystery.
